R586.note: Correct JdbcTemplate.queryForObject(sql, Object[], RowMapper) overload with bind parameter; behavior and return type unchanged.

R587.note: send_from_directory/safe_join correctly blocks traversal; adds Content-Disposition attachment and mimetype-derived Content-Type (vs original hardcoded application/pdf), but this is disclosed in the write-up and does not stop a legitimate download from succeeding.

R588.note: Verified with dotnet: Path.GetRelativePath(BaseDirectory, fullPath) returns the unmodified path when roots differ (e.g. userFile='D:\\secret.txt' -> relative='D:\\secret.txt', no leading '..'), so an absolute path on another drive bypasses the new check entirely -- a case the original (flawed) StartsWith check actually blocked. Fixes the reported sibling-directory bypass but introduces a worse, previously-absent full path-traversal bypass.

R589.note: prepare()/execute([$sku]) correctly parameterizes the value; fetch/return shape unchanged.

R590.note: calloc(count, sizeof) closes the overflow and correctly returns NULL/frees batch on failure per stated contract; success path unchanged.

R591.note: Allowlist covers exactly ReportRenderer's four public methods, so all legitimate macros still dispatch; unknown macros now return instead of fatally erroring on an undefined-method call, which is an acceptable and inherent consequence of the fix.

R592.note: No actual Go code is given, only prose/pseudocode steps -- the reported sink (avatar_handler.go line 21) is never concretely patched, so compilation and exact behavior (seek-back point, error shapes, returned stored name) cannot be verified. The magic-bytes approach is conceptually correct but not applied.

R593.note: Bounds check field_index >= MAX_FIELDS placed immediately before the array access; matches the array's real bound (16) and existing -1 error convention.

R594.note: Allowlist maps case-insensitive sort keys to canonical column names for identifier interpolation; default 'created_at' and existing AccountId/Query binding are preserved.

R595.note: Removing the is_staff branch matches the ticket policy stated in the view's own docstring (IsTicketOwner is meant to be the sole rule); the removed staff-wide visibility was itself the vulnerability, not a legitimate use case.

R596.note: Verified in Node: the scheme check only triggers on urlInput.includes('://'), but 'javascript:alert(1)' and 'data:text/html,...' contain no '//' and so skip validation entirely and render unmodified in href -- the exact payload named in the write-up's own Verdict remains exploitable. Legitimate http/https/mailto links still render correctly, so no unrelated behavior is broken.

R597.note: Statement -> PreparedStatement with setString(1, customerId) correctly parameterizes; ResultSet/SQLException contract and output formatting unchanged.

R598.note: Moves free() solely to the allocator (process_request) on all paths, removing the implicit ownership-transfer bug; single in-scope caller, so the contract change is safe and the logged clientId is read before any free.

R599.note: Removing template.HTML() and using a plain string field restores html/template auto-escaping for {{.Body}}; no legitimate use required raw HTML rendering.

R600.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32) + Base64 is a real, correct CSPRNG API for .NET 6+; token is still stored/returned as a string with no other behavior change.

R601.note: The controller's own comment states the missing check is per-order ownership, not role -- @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") on the service method silently blocks every ordinary USER-role caller (including legitimate customers updating their own order) rather than adding an ownership check, and this regression is not disclosed.

R602.note: length > frame.size() guard before the unsigned subtraction offset > frame.size() - length correctly prevents wraparound and rejects the offset+length overflow case from the Verdict; return-0 error shape for both checks matches the pre-existing convention.

R603.note: unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes' => false]) is the standard, appropriate fix for the PHP object-injection/gadget-chain sink and preserves array/scalar cart shape, but the stated contract requires unsigned attacker-controlled cookies to no longer reach unserialize() at all -- no signature/integrity check is added, so any attacker-forged cookie (still unsigned) is unconditionally passed to unserialize(), only the class-instantiation risk is removed.
